title: Streamed structured output checkpointing and idempotent replay for interleaved tool-calls
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement:

When the API streams structured JSON interleaved with tool/function calls (e.g., a top-level JSON object that contains fields populated by model-generated segments and by external tool responses), truncated responses, escapes inside strings, and mid-stream retries lead to inconsistent client-side state. Existing heuristics (heuristic reassembly, escape normalization) are insufficient when: (a) tool-call boundaries are nested or interleaved with JSON fragments, (b) the SDK cannot resume at an absolute token offset because different runtimes may re-tokenize differently, and (c) older SDKs do not understand resume tokens or checksums.

Goal:
Provide a deterministic, backwards-compatible checkpointing & idempotent replay mechanism for streaming structured outputs that: 1) allows safe truncation+retry across tool-call boundaries, 2) preserves JSON validity for older SDKs (best-effort), 3) avoids reprocessing side-effects from tool-calls during retries, and 4) provides clear failure modes and diagnostics for operators and customers.

Proposed design (high level):

1) Stream-level checkpoint messages (opaque to model payloads)
- Introduce a short structured control record that can be emitted at stable boundaries (end of top-level object field, or immediately after a tool-call completion). Control record syntax: ``@@checkpoint v1|seq=NN|cid=<sha256-chunk>|len=<byte-len>|cksum=<crc32>`` followed by newline. Control records are guaranteed to be emitted only at canonical framing boundaries (see framing rules).

2) Canonical framing rules
- Top-level tokens: define canonical cut points at top-level JSON value boundaries and immediately after tool-call result markers.
- Tool-call markers: tool-call start/end are annotated in the stream with explicit markers (``@@call-start id=...`` / ``@@call-end id=...``) so the runtime and client can deterministically identify side-effect regions.

3) Idempotent replay semantics
- Each tool-call is executed exactly-once per sequence id by default. The runtime emits a per-call replay token ``call-replay=<uuid>`` in the checkpoint control record. If a stream is retried from an earlier checkpoint, the server will attach ``call-replayed=true`` in the subsequent tool-call invocation metadata so tool adapters can detect and deduplicate execution.

4) Backward compatibility and graceful degradation
- Older SDKs that do not understand checkpoint control records will ignore lines beginning with ``@@`` and continue parsing as best-effort. We provide a compatibility mode where the server mirrors a safe small prefix of the last complete JSON object when a control record is present so naive parsers see a syntactically valid trailing object. This is a best-effort fallback, not a guarantee.

5) Escape handling and truncated strings
- Checkpoints include a small escape-state snapshot ("open_string": true/false and an escape buffer of the last up to 64 bytes) so the client can know whether the stream ended mid-string and whether it must request a resume that includes the escape buffer to avoid introducing invalid escape sequences.

6) Resume negotiation protocol
- On client-detected truncation/error, client sends a resume request with the last-observed checkpoint seq and cid. Server validates the checkpoint and either: (a) returns a resume segment (delta) starting exactly from the canonical boundary, or (b) rejects resume and falls back to full restart with a header explaining why (e.g., checkpoint aged out).

7) Observability and errors
- Emit metrics: checkpoint_emitted, checkpoint_skipped_boundary, resume_requested, resume_rejected_reason. Correlate with model-run id and customer id. Provide a trace link in the last checkpoint control record.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Checkpoint markers increase stream bandwidth slightly (small control line every ~1-4 KB configurable). Trade-off: stronger correctness vs small overhead.
- Deterministic framing requires server to be the arbiter of canonical cut points; clients must trust the server-specified resume tokens.
- Exactly-once tool-call semantics requires tool adapters to be idempotent-aware. For adapters that cannot dedupe, we include a best-effort shim that caches recent call results for a short TTL keyed by call-replay token. This can increase memory usage.

Acceptance criteria:
- Server can emit checkpoint control records at configured frequency and attach per-checkpoint metadata (seq, cid, cksum, open_string flag, last_escape_bytes).
- SDKs (JS, Python) can request resume using checkpoint tokens and reconstruct valid JSON without introducing syntax errors in >=95% fuzz tests for truncated streams with nested tool-calls.
- Tool adapter deduplication hook honored: when a resume indicates call-replayed=true, adapter receives metadata and does not double-execute side-effects; integration test demonstrates no duplicate writes for a mocked database adapter.
- Backward compatibility test: older SDKs ignoring ``@@`` markers do not crash on synthetic streams with mirrored safe-prefix enabled.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Replay tokens leak sensitive inputs in logs. Mitigation: tokens are opaque, short-lived, and redacted in logs by default; include KMS policy in design doc.
- Risk: Increased memory for replay cache. Mitigation: LRU eviction and per-customer quotas; document OOM boundaries.
- Risk: Clients may misinterpret control markers; mitigation: provide SDK parsers and clear spec, and a feature flag in Console to opt-in per workspace.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement server-side checkpoint emission behind feature flag (internal-only) and add metrics.
2) Implement SDK parsing/wrapper for resume in JS and Python; release canary packages.
3) End-to-end test harness with mocked tool adapters demonstrating dedupe and resume flows.
4) Beta with select customers/partners; gather feedback and harden.
5) Gradual GA and default-on for new streams after 6-week beta window.

Links to artifacts and PRs:
- Design doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/STREAM-CHECKPOINTING-2026
- Initial PoC repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/stream-checkpointing/pull/12
- SDK resume spec (draft): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1AbCdEfGhJkL-ResumeSpec

Monitoring & alerting:
- Create dashboard for checkpoint_emitted vs resume_requested ratio. Alert if resume_rejected_rate > 1% for >1h. Log sample traces for manual triage.

Open questions (for PM/SEC/Design):
- What workspace-level opt-in UX is acceptable for customers who require immutable side-effects? (PM)
- Should replay tokens be HSM-backed for high-security customers? (SEC)
- UI signal for Console to visualize checkpoint lineage and trace links (Design)
acceptance_criteria: 1) Control records emitted and documented; 2) SDKs can resume and reconstruct valid JSON in fuzz tests; 3) Tool adapters honor call-replayed metadata and dedupe; 4) Metrics and dashboard created; 5) Backward-compatibility fallback verified in integration tests
steps: Server: implement control-record emission and framing enforcement behind feature flag
Runtime: add call-replay token generation and per-call metadata plumbing
Adapters: add dedupe hook and short-lived result cache
SDKs: JS/Python resume parser + convenience helpers
Testing: fuzz truncated stream scenarios, nested tool-calls, escape edge cases
Docs: confluence spec, SDK changelog, migration guide
Rollout: internal canary -> beta customers -> GA
